name: MailboxSend
title: Send Mail
description: Send a message from a connected mailbox, or reply in a thread, with the words a previous step produced
whenToUse: Send an email a workflow composed rather than one a model decided to write: a report, a confirmation, a rendered template, the same message to each of a list. Every field takes a template, so the recipient, the subject and the body are bound to what earlier steps produced. Give it a message to answer and it replies in that conversation instead of starting a new one. It sends from the mailbox its credential connected, and it sends once, at the moment the graph reaches it.

outputs.name: sent
outputs.description: True when the mailbox accepted it

outputs.name: messageId
outputs.description: The sent message's id, for looking it up

to.title: To
to.description: Who it goes to. Separate several with commas. Leave blank when replying.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: The subject line. Ignored when replying, which keeps the conversation's own.

body.title: Body
body.description: The message itself, as plain text or HTML depending on Body Type. Ignored when Body Type is Design Template.

bodyType.title: Body Type
bodyType.description: How the message is written. Plain Text and HTML send the Body as typed. Design Template draws one of your templates instead and sends that, with a plain-text version alongside it for readers whose client shows no pictures.

template.title: Template
template.description: Which template to draw, scoped to its org, as in "sab/outreach-email". Only read when Body Type is Design Template.

content.title: What to write in
content.description: What goes into each part of the template, keyed by the part's name. The keys are the template's own sections, so { "subject": { "subject": "..." }, "opening": { "message": "..." } }. Any part left out draws with what its designer wrote as the default, so a half-filled template still sends a whole letter.

inReplyTo.title: In reply to
inReplyTo.description: A message id to answer. Given one, this replies in that conversation and the recipients and subject come from it. Blank starts a new one.

emitOnTestRun.title: Perform on test runs
emitOnTestRun.description: This step acts outside the platform and cannot be undone, so test runs trace it rather than perform it. Enable only while testing this step, then switch it off.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: mail
package.packageFile:
# MAIL — the platform's own mailbox (docs/unoverse/mail/README.md): an address in, a
# conversation out. Inboxes on the platform's domain, each a list of threads, each thread its
# messages in order; a reply goes back into the thread it answers.
#
# TWO NODES. MailboxMessages reads an inbox as a step; MailboxMCP gives an attached Agent the
# mailbox as tools: list the threads, read one, reply, send, draft. Both reach the mailbox
# service THROUGH THE ENGINE at loopback (`scope.engineUrl` + /mail/...), the way the document
# nodes reach /documents: a node's call must be https or loopback, and the engine holds the
# service. THE INBOX IS THE CREDENTIAL (credentials/mailboxCredential.yaml, owner ruling
# 2026-09-20): address, name and the AWS account that receives and sends for it, set once on
# the credentials screen. Both nodes name it; neither has an inbox field.
#
# NOT the `email` package. SendGridEmail is one-way mail with no thread; this is two-way and
# threaded, and a saved workflow storing either type keeps meaning what it meant.

name: mail
displayName: Mailbox
description: >-
  Read and answer email from an inbox of the platform's own: threads, messages, replies and
  drafts, for a step or for an Agent
version: 0.1.0
category: communication
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Read an inbox's threads, newest first, with each thread's last message
  - "Give an Agent the mailbox as tools: list, read, reply, send, draft"
  - A reply carries In-Reply-To and References, so it lands in the same conversation everywhere

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK ONLY, numeric form: every call goes to the engine's own listener, which serves the
  # mailbox. No third-party host, ever.
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]

credentials.googleClientCredential.yaml:
# THE PLATFORM'S ONE GOOGLE APPLICATION, saved once and never again.
#
# NOBODY CHOOSES THIS, which is why `visibility: internal` keeps it out of the credentials
# picker. It is collected in the panel that opens under the Connect button, the first time
# anyone on this platform connects a Gmail mailbox, and never seen again.
#
# It is a credential rather than a setting so it is encrypted at rest with everything else, and
# so it can be saved from the screen a person is already standing on instead of by editing a
# file and restarting.

name: googleClientCredential
displayName: Google application
category: Platform setup
visibility: internal
description: The OAuth client that makes Google's approval screen say unoverse. Collected once, under the Connect button.
documentationUrl: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials

properties:
  - name: clientId
    displayName: Client ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: From the OAuth client you created in Google Cloud.
    placeholder: 1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com

  - name: clientSecret
    displayName: Client secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: From the same page.
    placeholder: ""
credentials.mailboxCredential.yaml:
# PICK THE SERVICE, LOG IN, DONE (owner ruling 2026-09-20: "stop overcomplicating"; "I should
# see Outlook, I should see Gmail"). The same shape as adding an account on a phone: name it,
# choose Gmail or Outlook, approve on their own screen. Everything else comes back from them
# and is never typed.
#
# The Agent then acts on that mailbox with nobody signed in, which is what the grant is for —
# the same way a phone keeps fetching mail long after you logged into it once.

name: mailboxCredential
displayName: Mailbox
category: Communication
description: A mailbox an Agent reads and answers. Connect Gmail or Outlook.

properties:
  - name: connect
    displayName: Mailbox
    type: connect
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Choose where the mailbox lives and approve access on their screen.
    connect: /mail/connect
    connected: address
    providers:
      - { id: google, label: Gmail }
      - { id: microsoft, label: Outlook }

  # ── Filled by the service when you connect. Never typed, never shown again. ─────────────
  - name: address
    displayName: Address
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: The mailbox you connected.
    "ui:dependencies": { __never: true }

  - name: provider
    displayName: Service
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Which service holds it.
    "ui:dependencies": { __never: true }

  - name: refreshToken
    displayName: Grant
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: The lasting permission this mailbox gave.
    "ui:dependencies": { __never: true }

shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA: what an attached Agent reads before touching the mailbox. The
# wording IS the routing: a model reads these descriptions when choosing a tool, so rephrasing
# is a behaviour change, never a tidy-up. The argument shapes are what the model fills in.
#
# Written as plain YAML rather than a `return { ... }` expression: a constant is data.

mailbox:
  name: Mailbox
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: One email inbox, as threads and messages. Read what is waiting, answer in the thread, start a message, keep a draft.
  instructions: |-
    MAILBOX PROTOCOL:
    - list_threads first, to see what is waiting. It is cheap and carries no bodies.
    - read_thread before answering anything: a reply is judged against the whole conversation,
      not its last line.
    - reply answers IN the thread, to the person who wrote, with the others copied. Use it for
      every answer to a message you have read. Never start a new message to answer an old one.
    - send starts a NEW conversation with someone; only for a message that answers nothing.
    - save_draft when a person should look before it goes. A draft is not sent.
    - A sent message comes back with state "sent" and its id. State "failed" carries the reason;
      say so rather than claiming it went.
    - You work ONE inbox. You cannot read or send from any other.
  methods:
    list_threads:
      description: >-
        The conversations in the inbox, newest first, each with its subject, who is in it, how
        many messages, when the last one arrived, and that last message's sender and direction.
        No bodies: read_thread gives those. An empty list means nothing is waiting, which is
        normal.
      input:
        type: object
        required: []
        properties:
          since:
            type: string
            description: Only threads with a message after this time, as an ISO date. Leave out for the newest regardless.
          limit:
            type: number
            description: How many threads, newest first. Default 20, at most 200.
    read_thread:
      description: >-
        One conversation in full: every message in order, each with sender, recipients,
        subject, the text, and its attachments as links that open for a while. Call it before
        replying.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [threadId]
        properties:
          threadId:
            type: string
            description: The thread's id, from list_threads.
    reply:
      description: >-
        Answer a message in its own thread. The reply goes to the message's sender, with the
        other people on it copied, under the thread's subject, and carries the headers that make
        it land in the same conversation in their mail client. Comes back with state "sent" and
        the message's id, or "failed" with the reason.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [messageId, text]
        properties:
          messageId:
            type: string
            description: The id of the message being answered, from read_thread. Usually the last one from the other side.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The reply, as plain text. Write the whole message; it is sent as written.
          html:
            type: string
            description: Optional. The same reply as HTML, when the message needs formatting. The text is still sent alongside.
    send:
      description: >-
        Start a NEW conversation: a message from the inbox to one or more people. Not for
        answering a message, which is reply. Comes back with state "sent" and the message's id,
        or "failed" with the reason.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [to, subject, text]
        properties:
          to:
            type: string
            description: Who it goes to, one or more addresses separated by commas. A name may be given as "Name <address>".
          cc:
            type: string
            description: Optional. Who is copied, the same way.
          subject:
            type: string
            description: The subject line.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The message, as plain text.
          html:
            type: string
            description: Optional. The same message as HTML.
    save_draft:
      description: >-
        Keep a message without sending it, for a person to read and send. Comes back with state
        "draft" and the draft's id. Nothing leaves the inbox.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [to, subject, text]
        properties:
          to:
            type: string
            description: Who it is for, one or more addresses separated by commas.
          cc:
            type: string
            description: Optional. Who would be copied.
          subject:
            type: string
            description: The subject line.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The message, as plain text.
          html:
            type: string
            description: Optional. The same message as HTML.

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order. Whichever call ran is the one that
# answered, so each row reads both and takes the one that is there.

- emit: sent
  value: "return ((calls.reply || calls.send || {}).state) === 'sent'"

- emit: messageId
  value: "return (calls.reply || calls.send || {}).id || ''"

- emit: threadId
  value: "return (calls.reply || calls.send || {}).threadId || ''"
files.api/run.yaml:
# TWO DOORS, ONE NODE, chosen by whether it is answering something. A reply must go through the
# mailbox's own reply so it lands in the conversation and threads in the recipient's client; a
# new message cannot use it, because there is nothing to answer.
#
# `when` means the unchosen call never runs, so its key is absent and the events table reads
# whichever one did.

- name: reply
  when: "return !!String(config.inReplyTo || '').trim()"
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/messages/'
      + encodeURIComponent(String(credentials.mailboxCredential.address || '').trim().toLowerCase())
      + '/' + encodeURIComponent(String(config.inReplyTo).trim()) + '/reply'
  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 30000
  body:
    # A DESIGNED REPLY sends the template and what goes in it; the door draws it and
    # produces both the HTML and the plain-text twin, so neither can drift from the other.
    template: "return config.bodyType === 'template' ? (String(config.template || '').trim() || undefined) : undefined"
    content: "return config.bodyType === 'template' ? (config.content || {}) : undefined"
    text: "return config.bodyType === 'template' ? undefined : (config.bodyType === 'html' ? '' : String(config.body || ''))"
    html: "return config.bodyType === 'html' ? String(config.body || '') : undefined"
    cc: "return String(config.cc || '').trim() || undefined"
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error"

- name: send
  when: "return !String(config.inReplyTo || '').trim()"
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/inboxes/'
      + encodeURIComponent(String(credentials.mailboxCredential.address || '').trim().toLowerCase())
      + '/messages'
  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 30000
  body:
    to: "{{ config.to }}"
    cc: "return String(config.cc || '').trim() || undefined"
    subject: "{{ config.subject }}"
    template: "return config.bodyType === 'template' ? (String(config.template || '').trim() || undefined) : undefined"
    content: "return config.bodyType === 'template' ? (config.content || {}) : undefined"
    text: "return config.bodyType === 'template' ? undefined : (config.bodyType === 'html' ? '' : String(config.body || ''))"
    html: "return config.bodyType === 'html' ? String(config.body || '') : undefined"
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error"
files.config.yaml:
# EVERY FIELD TAKES A TEMPLATE (`ui:field: template`), which is how a step sends what an earlier
# one produced: bind the body to a rendered template, the recipient to a row's address, the
# subject to a fund's name. A literal typed in works too.
configSchema:
  type: object
  # A MESSAGE NEEDS A SUBJECT AND SOMETHING TO SAY, but the something has two sources now:
  # a Body typed here, or a Design Template drawn by the door. Requiring `body` outright
  # made a templated message impossible to configure — the form demanded a field the send
  # would then ignore. The door is what knows whether a message is empty, and it says so.
  required: [subject]
  properties:
    to:
      type: string
      title: To
      description: Who it goes to. Separate several with commas. Leave blank when replying.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    cc:
      type: string
      title: CC
      description: Copied recipients, comma-separated
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    subject:
      type: string
      title: Subject
      description: The subject line. Ignored when replying, which keeps the conversation's own.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    body:
      type: string
      title: Body
      description: >-
        The message itself, as plain text or HTML depending on Body Type. Ignored when Body
        Type is Design Template.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    bodyType:
      type: string
      title: Body Type
      description: >-
        How the message is written. Plain Text and HTML send the Body as typed. Design
        Template draws one of your templates instead and sends that, with a plain-text
        version alongside it for readers whose client shows no pictures.
      default: text
      enum: [text, html, template]
      enumNames: [Plain Text, HTML, Design Template]

    template:
      type: string
      title: Template
      description: >-
        Which template to draw, scoped to its org, as in "sab/outreach-email". Only read
        when Body Type is Design Template.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: [template] }

    content:
      type: object
      title: What to write in
      description: >-
        What goes into each part of the template, keyed by the part's name. The keys are
        the template's own sections, so { "subject": { "subject": "..." }, "opening":
        { "message": "..." } }. Any part left out draws with what its designer wrote as
        the default, so a half-filled template still sends a whole letter.
      default: {}
      ui:field: template
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: [template] }

    inReplyTo:
      type: string
      title: In reply to
      description: >-
        A message id to answer. Given one, this replies in that conversation and the recipients
        and subject come from it. Blank starts a new one.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
"ui:order": [to, cc, subject, bodyType, body, template, content, inReplyTo]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    required: true
    description: Trigger to fire the node

outputs:
  - name: sent
    type: boolean
    description: True when the mailbox accepted it
  - name: messageId
    type: string
    description: The sent message's id, for looking it up
  - name: threadId
    type: string
    description: The conversation it landed in

# WHICH MAILBOX IT SENDS FROM is the credential's, never a field here: the same connection the
# Agent reads with, so a reply comes from the address the message arrived at.
credentials:
  - name: mailboxCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Mailbox
files.node.yaml:
type: MailboxSend
kind: PromiseNode

name: Send Mail
category: Communication
color: "#0F766E"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  Send a message from a connected mailbox, or reply in a thread, with the words a previous step
  produced

# Outcome first, disqualify by PROPERTY, never name another node, wiring last.
whenToUse: >-
  Send an email a workflow composed rather than one a model decided to write: a report, a
  confirmation, a rendered template, the same message to each of a list. Every field takes a
  template, so the recipient, the subject and the body are bound to what earlier steps produced.
  Give it a message to answer and it replies in that conversation instead of starting a new one.
  It sends from the mailbox its credential connected, and it sends once, at the moment the graph
  reaches it.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable: sending is the side effect. A cached answer would report a delivered message
  # that was never sent, which is the worst possible lie for a node whose whole purpose is that
  # something left the building.
  cacheable: false

  # The same fact, positively, so the ENGINE can act on it: mail that has reached a mailbox has
  # no inverse. A test run traces what this would have sent and does not send it, because a build
  # calls runTest after every stage and each one would otherwise reach a real person.
  emitsExternally: true
files.test.yaml:
# DELIBERATELY NOT A REAL SEND. This node puts a message in a real person's inbox and that has
# no inverse, so the fixture names an address nobody owns and asserts the SHAPE of the refusal:
# a bench that mails someone every time it runs is not one anyone runs twice.
#
# The engine also withholds this node on a test run (capabilities.emitsExternally), so a build
# traces what it would have sent rather than sending it.
testData:
  config:
    to: "nobody@test.invalid"
    subject: "Bench"
    bodyType: text
    body: "Sent by the node bench."

  inputs:
    signal: {}

  expect:
    sent: "return typeof output.sent === 'boolean'"
    messageId: "return typeof output.messageId === 'string'"
